symbols.name: m
symbols.def: A fixed integer that does not vary with \(n\).

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: A fixed fold count that does not vary with \(n\).

symbols.name: \mathcal I_k
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_1,\ldots,\mathcal I_K\) is a deterministic partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with fold sizes differing by at most one.

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)^\top\) is supplied by the target-population registry.

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: The supplied population fraction that must receive treatment.

symbols.name: C_Y
symbols.def: A fixed almost-sure bound for both potential outcomes.

symbols.name: \overline\omega
symbols.def: A fixed upper eigenvalue bound with \(\underline\omega<\overline\omega\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{kl}
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{kl}(a,s)=a\log(a/s)+(1-a)\log((1-a)/(1-s))\) on \([0,1]^2\), with \(0\log(0/x)=0\) for every \(x\in[0,1]\), \(x\log(x/0)=+\infty\) for every \(x>0\), and the sum taken in the extended nonnegative reals. Thus \(\operatorname{kl}(0,0)=\operatorname{kl}(1,1)=0\), \(\operatorname{kl}(a,0)=+\infty\) for \(a>0\), and \(\operatorname{kl}(a,1)=+\infty\) for \(a<1\).

symbols.name: u_j
symbols.def: The \(j\)-th standard basis vector of \(\mathbb R^m\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: The ambient orthonormal frame is fixed as part of \(\mathfrak G\): \(B^\top B=I_d\), \(B^\top p=0\), and its ordered columns are not subsequently rotated.

symbols.name: \Omega
symbols.def: The positive-definite covariance matrix expressed in the fixed \(B\)-coordinates of \(\mathfrak G\).

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(Q=\Omega^{1/2}B^\top\), with the principal symmetric square root and the fixed frame supplied by \(\mathfrak G\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak G
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak G=(m,p,q,b,\kappa;B,\Omega;Q,\mathcal A,H)\) is the framed ambient geometry. Its definition attaches the canonically derived chart collection without adding a freely rotatable coordinate choice.

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: Generic mean of the canonical Gaussian contact experiment.

symbols.name: \mathcal G
symbols.def: A generic finite subset of the Gaussian parameter space.

symbols.name: \mathscr D
symbols.def: The quotient of all Borel maps \(\bar\delta:\mathbb R^d\to\mathcal A\), where \(\bar\delta_1\sim\bar\delta_2\) when they agree Lebesgue almost everywhere.

symbols.name: \delta
symbols.def: A generic equivalence class of Borel exactly feasible assignment maps.

symbols.name: \delta^\star
symbols.def: A symbol bound only by \(\mathrm{prop{:}minimax\text{-}selector\text{-}binding}\) after the affirmative conclusion of \(\mathrm{oeq{:}global\text{-}minimax\text{-}existence}\); it has no referent otherwise.

symbols.name: \delta^{\mathrm{sc}}_\kappa
symbols.def: The essentially unique scalar rule asserted by \(\mathrm{thm{:}scalar\text{-}reverse\text{-}kl\text{-}saddle}\).

symbols.name: \pi_\kappa
symbols.def: A proper least-favorable distribution for the scalar reverse-KL game at temperature \(\kappa\).

symbols.name: F
symbols.type: exposed face of the capacity polytope
symbols.def: A nonempty exposed face \(F=\arg\max_{a\in\mathcal A}v^\top Qa\) for some \(v\in\mathbb R^d\), interpreted with the chart supplied by \(\mathfrak G\).

symbols.name: E
symbols.def: A generic exposed face \(E\subsetneq F\); the same framed construction is applied to this face.

symbols.name: B_F
symbols.def: The ordered orthonormal basis of \(\operatorname{lin}(F-F)\) produced by lexicographically signed Gram--Schmidt from \(u_1,\ldots,u_m\); it is the \(B_F\)-component of \(\mathfrak G\).

symbols.name: \mathscr D_F
symbols.def: The quotient by Lebesgue almost-everywhere equality in \(\mathbb R^{r_F}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_F
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak R_F=\{\delta_F\in\mathscr D_F:\sup_{\theta\in\mathbb R^{r_F}}R_F(\theta,\delta_F)=r_F^{\min}\}\); the definition does not assert nonemptiness.

symbols.name: \delta_F^{\min}
symbols.def: When \(r_F=1\), the Borel representative whose existence and essential uniqueness are asserted by \(\mathrm{thm{:}scalar\text{-}reverse\text{-}kl\text{-}saddle}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal N_F^\circ
symbols.def: \(\mathcal N_F^\circ=\{v\in\mathbb R^d:\lVert v\rVert_2=1,\ F=\arg\max_{a\in\mathcal A}v^\top Qa\}\), the relative interior of the corresponding spherical normal cone.

symbols.name: \mathfrak T_{\mathfrak G}
symbols.def: For \(L,\rho>0\), \(v\in\mathcal N_F^\circ\), \(\delta\in\mathscr D\), and \(\delta_F\in\mathscr D_F\), set \[d^{\mathfrak G}_{F,L,\rho,v}(\delta,\delta_F)^2=\sup_{\lVert\theta\rVert_2\le L}\mathbb E_{Z\sim N_d(\rho v+J_F\theta,I_d)}\!\left[\lVert D_p^{1/2}\{\delta(Z)-\delta_F(J_F^\top Z)\}\rVert_2^2\right].\] For \(E\subsetneq F\), put \(J_{E\mid F}=J_F^\top J_E\); for every unit \(w\in\mathbb R^{r_F}\) with \(E=\arg\max_{a\in F}w^\top G_F^{1/2}B_F^\top(a-a_F^0)\), set \[d^{\mathfrak G}_{E\mid F,L,\rho,w}(\delta_F,\delta_E)^2=\sup_{\lVert\theta\rVert_2\le L}\mathbb E_{Z_F\sim N_{r_F}(\rho w+J_{E\mid F}\theta,I_{r_F})}\!\left[\lVert D_p^{1/2}\{\delta_F(Z_F)-\delta_E(J_{E\mid F}^\top Z_F)\}\rVert_2^2\right].\] Full-to-face convergence and nested-face compatibility mean that these displayed quantities tend to zero as \(\rho\to\infty\), for every fixed \(L\) and displayed direction. Gaussian densities make both quantities invariant to the chosen almost-everywhere representatives.

symbols.name: \rho_F
symbols.def: For any \(a\in F\), let \(J_F=\{j:a_j\text{ is nonconstant on }F\}\), \(q_F=q-\sum_{j\notin J_F}p_ja_j\), and \(p_F=\sum_{j\in J_F}p_j\). Then \(\rho_F=\min\{q_F,p_F-q_F\}\); the fixed coordinates make this independent of the selected \(a\in F\).

symbols.name: \mathsf E_F
symbols.def: The transported identity-covariance face decision problem whose complete chart is supplied by \(\mathfrak G\) and displayed in \(\mathrm{def{:}face\text{-}experiment}\).

symbols.name: \sigma
symbols.def: The fixed-coordinate value indexing an oriented edge.

symbols.name: E_{j,\sigma}
symbols.type: oriented edge of the three-cell capacity hexagon

symbols.name: n_{j,\sigma}
symbols.type: oriented unit normal in Gaussian parameter space
symbols.def: In \(\mathfrak G_3\), \(n_{j,\sigma}=(2\sigma-1)\Omega^{-1/2}B^\top u_j/\lVert\Omega^{-1/2}B^\top u_j\rVert_2\); this unit vector exposes exactly \(E_{j,\sigma}\).

symbols.name: t_{j,\sigma}
symbols.type: oriented unit tangent in Gaussian parameter space
symbols.def: Let \(j^-<j^+\) be the two indices distinct from \(j\), set \(B_{E_{j,\sigma}}=(u_{j^-}-u_{j^+})/\sqrt2\), and define \(t_{j,\sigma}=QB_{E_{j,\sigma}}/\lVert QB_{E_{j,\sigma}}\rVert_2=J_{E_{j,\sigma}}\). This fixes the edge orientation from \(j^+\) toward \(j^-\).

symbols.name: \delta^{F}_{j,\sigma}
symbols.type: canonical minimax rule on an oriented edge
symbols.def: \(\delta^{F}_{j,\sigma}=\delta^{\min}_{E_{j,\sigma}}\), the essentially unique one-dimensional minimax rule of the exact chart \(\Gamma_{E_{j,\sigma}}\) constructed by \(\mathrm{thm{:}scalar\text{-}reverse\text{-}kl\text{-}saddle}\); its input is \(t_{j,\sigma}^\top Z\).

symbols.name: T_{\mathrm e}
symbols.def: The lower normal displacement at which an edge-extension certificate begins.

symbols.name: U_{\mathrm e}
symbols.def: The absolute tangential offset covered by an edge-extension certificate.

symbols.name: \mathcal E_{j,\sigma}
symbols.def: The six residuals defined by \(\mathrm{def{:}oriented\text{-}edge\text{-}residuals}\), indexed by \((j,\sigma)\in\{1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}\).

symbols.name: \mathsf{EdgeCert}
symbols.def: The rational interval predicate constructed in \(\mathrm{def{:}oriented\text{-}edge\text{-}residuals}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{\mathrm{diag}}
symbols.def: In the fixed \(B\)-coordinates of \(\mathfrak G\), for \(c=(c_1,\ldots,c_d)\in(0,\infty)^d\) put \(A_c=\operatorname{diag}(c_1,\ldots,c_d)\) and \(\delta_c(z)=s(A_cz)\). Then \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{diag}}(\mathfrak G)=\{\delta_c:c\in(0,\infty)^d\}\subset\mathscr D\).

symbols.name: L_{\mathrm{in}}
symbols.def: The total binary encoding length of a framed geometry \(\mathfrak G\) with \(p,q\) rational and every entry of \(b,\kappa,B,\Omega\) rational or real algebraic, where a real-algebraic entry is encoded by its minimal polynomial and a rational isolating interval.

symbols.name: \underline r_\eta
symbols.def: A generic rational lower-value component associated with tolerance \(\eta\), without a validity guarantee built into the notation.

symbols.name: \overline r_\eta
symbols.def: A generic rational upper-value component associated with tolerance \(\eta\), without a validity guarantee built into the notation.

symbols.name: \mathbb B_{\mathcal A}
symbols.def: The decidable set of finite bitstrings encoding a rational polyhedral partition of \(\mathbb R^d\), rational arithmetic circuits on its cells, and a capacity-preserving final coordinate, with the decoded limit in \(\mathcal A\) at every input.

symbols.name: c_\eta
symbols.def: A generic finite bitstring associated with tolerance \(\eta\), without an accuracy guarantee built into the notation.

symbols.name: \operatorname{Dec}
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Dec}(c)\) is the Borel \(\mathcal A\)-valued limit map specified by the rational partition and circuits encoded by \(c\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{Eval}
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Eval}(c,z,L)\) executes the encoded circuit with directed rational rounding and a capacity-preserving final coordinate, returns \(a\in\mathcal A\cap\mathbb Q^m\), and guarantees \(\lVert D_p^{1/2}[a-\operatorname{Dec}(c)(z)]\rVert_2\le2^{-L}\).

symbols.name: d_{\mathrm{EKL}}
symbols.def: \(d_{\mathrm{EKL}}(\delta_1,\delta_2)=\sup_{h\in\mathbb R^d}\mathbb E_h[\kappa\sum_{j=1}^mp_j\operatorname{kl}(\delta_{1j}(Z),\delta_{2j}(Z))]\) as an extended nonnegative expectation using the total \(\operatorname{kl}\) on \([0,1]^2\); it equals \(+\infty\) when a boundary mismatch with infinite pointwise divergence occurs on a set of positive Gaussian probability for some \(h\).

symbols.name: \delta_\eta
symbols.type: conditionally bound certified feasible Gaussian rule
symbols.def: A symbol bound only by \(\mathrm{prop{:}certificate\text{-}output\text{-}binding}\) to the decoded output of a proved certificate; it has no referent otherwise.

symbols.name: \mathsf{Cert}_\eta
symbols.type: candidate finite-code Gaussian minimax certificate procedure
symbols.def: The finite-code value-and-map procedure specified by \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}handle}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal O
symbols.def: The measurable sample space for a cell label, treatment, and observed outcome.

symbols.name: \mathcal W
symbols.def: The measurable sample space for a cell label, treatment, and both potential outcomes.

symbols.name: \mathbb P
symbols.def: A probability law for \(W\) whose observed-data image is obtained by consistency.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: The law of \(O=(X,D,Y(D))\) induced by \(\mathbb P\).

symbols.name: \chi
symbols.type: efficient influence vector for the contact contrast

symbols.name: P_0
symbols.def: A baseline observed-data law at which \(\gamma(P_0)=0\) and \(\Omega=B^\top D_pV(P_0)D_pB\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak F_m
symbols.def: The full-data law class constructed in \(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}data\text{-}model}\).

symbols.name: \mathbb P_0
symbols.def: The conditionally independent potential-outcome lift of \(P_0\) constructed in \(\mathrm{def{:}product\text{-}coupling\text{-}lift}\).
symbols.role: full-data baseline for the least-favorable path

symbols.name: \mathbb P_{n,h}
symbols.def: The normalized conditional exponential tilt of \(\mathbb P_0\) constructed in \(\mathrm{def{:}conditional\text{-}tilt\text{-}path}\).

symbols.name: P_{n,h}
symbols.def: The observed-data image of \(\mathbb P_{n,h}\) under \(O=(X,D,Y(D))\).

symbols.name: \widehat\gamma
symbols.def: The measurable clipped finite-cell estimator constructed in \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}fitted\text{-}statistics}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Omega
symbols.def: The eigenvalue-clipped empirical covariance constructed in \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}fitted\text{-}statistics}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Omega^{\mathbb Q}
symbols.def: The measurable dyadic rounding of \(\widehat\Omega\) constructed in \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}fitted\text{-}statistics}\), with \(\lVert\widehat\Omega^{\mathbb Q}-\widehat\Omega\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le n^{-2}\).
symbols.role: finite covariance input to the certificate

symbols.name: \widehat a_n
symbols.def: The exactly feasible candidate action obtained by decoding the finite map code returned by \(\mathsf{Cert}_{\eta_n}\) and evaluating it at the contact statistic whitened by \(\widehat\Omega^{\mathbb Q}\).

symbols.name: a_n
symbols.def: Any Borel action based on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) that is exactly capacity-feasible.

symbols.name: \mathsf{Learner}_n
symbols.def: The exactly feasible learner construction in \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}fitted\text{-}learner\text{-}handle}\).

symbols.name: \nu_n
symbols.def: \(\nu_n(A)=\operatorname{Vol}(\{h:\lVert h\rVert\le M_n\})^{-1}\int_{\lVert h\rVert\le M_n}\Pr_{Z\sim N_d(h,I_d)}(Z\in A)\,dh\).

symbols.name: \mathsf K_n
symbols.def: \(\mathsf K_n(\delta_1,\delta_2)=\int\kappa\sum_{j=1}^m p_j\operatorname{kl}(\delta_{1j}(z),\delta_{2j}(z))\,\nu_n(dz)\) as an extended nonnegative integral using the total \(\operatorname{kl}\) on \([0,1]^2\); it equals \(+\infty\) when a boundary mismatch with infinite pointwise divergence has positive \(\nu_n\)-measure.

symbols.name: c_{\alpha_0}
symbols.def: \(c_{\alpha_0}=2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha_0/2)\min_{1\le j\le m}s_j(0)\sqrt{d\,\underline\omega}\). Positivity follows from the interior oracle and the covariance lower bound.

symbols.name: \mathcal C_n
symbols.type: joint policy and welfare confidence set
symbols.def: The set constructed in \(\mathrm{def{:}confidence\text{-}set\text{-}handle}\), with policy coordinate in \(\mathscr D\) and welfare coordinate \(v_n^\star(P)\).

novel.justification: All-cell contact describes scarce-allocation settings in which the registry cells have equal mass-weighted treatment effects at the local center, as under a common-effect baseline or a policy boundary calibrated before local heterogeneity is resolved. It is the explicit nonregular regime studied here, not a conclusion about the minimax rule.

definitions.name: \mathfrak F_m
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak F_m=\{\mathbb P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal W):\mathrm{ass{:}known\text{-}cell\text{-}masses},\mathrm{ass{:}conditional\text{-}ignorability},\mathrm{ass{:}overlap},\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes},\mathrm{ass{:}full\text{-}contact},\mathrm{ass{:}covariance\text{-}bounds}\text{ hold for the induced observed law }P\text{ at this fixed }m\}\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak M_{m}
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_m=\{P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal O):\mathrm{ass{:}known\text{-}cell\text{-}masses},\mathrm{ass{:}overlap},\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes},\mathrm{ass{:}full\text{-}contact},\mathrm{ass{:}covariance\text{-}bounds}\text{ hold for this fixed }m\}\).

definitions.name: \mathbb P_0
definitions.construction: For \(P_0\in\mathfrak M_m\), give \(Y(t)\mid X=j\) the \(P_0\)-law of \(Y\mid D=t,X=j\), impose \(Y(0)\perp_{\mathbb P_0}Y(1)\mid X\), draw \(D\mid X=j\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e_j)\) independently of both potential outcomes, and set \(Y=Y(D)\); this unique product-coupling lift induces exactly \(P_0\).

definitions.name: \mathbb P_{n,h}
definitions.construction: For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let \(A_{t,n}(X;h)=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_0}[\exp\{n^{-1/2}g_t(W;h)\}\mid X]\). Define the full-data path by \[\frac{d\mathbb P_{n,h}}{d\mathbb P_0}(W)=\prod_{t=0}^1\frac{\exp\{n^{-1/2}g_t(W;h)\}}{A_{t,n}(X;h)},\qquad P_{n,h}=\mathbb P_{n,h}\circ O^{-1}.\] The bounded-outcome condition makes every normalizer finite and strictly positive.

definitions.name: \operatorname{Regret}_n
definitions.construction: For any observed-data law \(P\) and action \(a\in\mathcal A\), set \(\mathcal W_n(P,a)=\sum_{j=1}^m p_ja_j\tau_j(P)-\lambda_nH(a)\), \(a_n^\circ(P)=\arg\max_{u\in\mathcal A}\mathcal W_n(P,u)\), and \(\operatorname{Regret}_n(a;P)=\mathcal W_n(P,a_n^\circ(P))-\mathcal W_n(P,a)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak G
definitions.construction: Fix once and for all the ordered matrix \(B\) satisfying \(B^\top B=I_d\) and \(B^\top p=0\), express \(\Omega\) in those coordinates, and set \(Q=\Omega^{1/2}B^\top\), \(\mathcal A=\{a\in[0,1]^m:p^\top a=q\}\), and \(H(a)=\sum_{j=1}^mp_j\operatorname{kl}(a_j,b_j)\). Attach to every exposed face \(F\) the complete chart \(\Gamma_F\) and the compatibility topology \(\mathfrak T_{\mathfrak G}\) displayed in \(\mathrm{def{:}face\text{-}experiment}\). Thus changing \(B\) changes \(\mathfrak G\), rather than silently re-expressing \(\Omega\), a comparator, or a ray.

definitions.name: s
definitions.construction:
For \(h\in\mathbb R^d\), solve the unique scalar equation \(\sum_{j=1}^m p_j\operatorname{expit}(\operatorname{logit}(b_j)+(p_j^{-1}(B\Omega^{1/2}h)_j-
u)/\kappa)=q\) for \(
u\), and set \(s_j(h)=\operatorname{expit}(\operatorname{logit}(b_j)+(p_j^{-1}(B\Omega^{1/2}h)_j-
u)/\kappa)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak R
definitions.construction: For the framed geometry \(\mathfrak G\), let \(\mathscr D=\{\bar\delta:\mathbb R^d\to\mathcal A\text{ Borel}\}/\!\sim\), \(r=\inf_{\bar\delta\in\mathscr D}\sup_{h\in\mathbb R^d}R(h,\bar\delta)\), and \(\mathfrak R=\{\bar\delta\in\mathscr D:\sup_hR(h,\bar\delta)=r\}\), where equivalence is Lebesgue almost-everywhere equality. No existence or uniqueness is included in this definition.

definitions.name: \mathsf E_F
definitions.construction: For each nonempty exposed face \(F\) of the framed geometry \(\mathfrak G\), let \(r_F=\dim(F)\), \(a_F^0=\arg\min_{a\in\operatorname{aff}(F)}\lVert a\rVert_2\), and let \(B_F\) be lexicographically signed Gram--Schmidt applied to the standard coordinate vectors after orthogonal projection onto \(\operatorname{lin}(F-F)\). Define \(\mathcal X_F=\{x:a_F^0+B_Fx\in F\}\), \(G_F=B_F^\top Q^\top QB_F\), and \(J_F=QB_FG_F^{-1/2}\). Then \(J_F^\top J_F=I_{r_F}\), the affine action chart is \(x\mapsto a_F^0+B_Fx\), and the observation chart is \(z\mapsto z_F=J_F^\top z\). The transported experiment is \(Z_F\sim N_{r_F}(\theta,I_{r_F})\), with \(s_F(\theta)=a_F^0+B_F\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X_F}\{\theta^\top G_F^{1/2}x-\kappa H(a_F^0+B_Fx)\}\), \(\delta_F^{\mathrm{plug}}(z_F)=s_F(z_F)\), \(\ell_F(\theta,a)=\theta^\top G_F^{1/2}B_F^\top[s_F(\theta)-a]-\kappa H(s_F(\theta))+\kappa H(a)\), and \(R_F(\theta,\delta_F)=\mathbb E_\theta[\ell_F(\theta,\delta_F(Z_F))]\). The quotient \(\mathscr D_F\), value \(r_F^{\min}\), correspondence \(\mathfrak R_F\), normal stratum \(\mathcal N_F^\circ\), and both metrics defining \(\mathfrak T_{\mathfrak G}\) are exactly those displayed in the symbol table. For \(r_F=0\), use the unique \(m\times0\) matrix \(B_F\), \(\mathcal X_F=\{0\}\), the empty identity \(G_F=I_0\), the unique \(d\times0\) isometry \(J_F\), the point observation, and the constant action equal to the unique vertex \(F\); these conventions make every displayed chart literal for vertices as well as positive-dimensional faces.

definitions.name: \mathfrak G_3
definitions.construction: Set \(m=3\), \(p=(1/3,1/3,1/3)\), \(q=1/2\), \(b=(1/2,1/2,1/2)\), \[B=\begin{bmatrix}1/\sqrt2&1/\sqrt6\\-1/\sqrt2&1/\sqrt6\\0&-2/\sqrt6\end{bmatrix},\qquad\Omega=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&4\end{bmatrix},\qquad Q=\Omega^{1/2}B^\top.\] For \(E_{j,\sigma}=\{a\in\mathcal A:a_j=\sigma\}\), let \(j^-<j^+\) be the remaining indices, \(B_{E_{j,\sigma}}=(u_{j^-}-u_{j^+})/\sqrt2\), \(t_{j,\sigma}=QB_{E_{j,\sigma}}/\lVert QB_{E_{j,\sigma}}\rVert_2\), and \(n_{j,\sigma}=(2\sigma-1)\Omega^{-1/2}B^\top u_j/\lVert\Omega^{-1/2}B^\top u_j\rVert_2\). Then \(t_{j,\sigma}=J_{E_{j,\sigma}}\), \(t_{j,\sigma}^\top n_{j,\sigma}=0\), and \(E_{j,\sigma}=\arg\max_{a\in\mathcal A}n_{j,\sigma}^\top Qa\) for all six oriented pairs.

definitions.name: (\mathcal E_{j,\sigma},\mathsf{EdgeCert})
definitions.construction: In the single Helmert-framed experiment \(\mathfrak G_3\), for each \(j\in\{1,2,3\}\), \(\sigma\in\{0,1\}\), \(\bar\delta\in\mathscr D\), and \(T_{\mathrm e},U_{\mathrm e}>0\), define \[\mathcal E_{j,\sigma}(\bar\delta;T_{\mathrm e},U_{\mathrm e})=\sup_{\rho\ge T_{\mathrm e},\,|x|\le U_{\mathrm e}}\left\{\mathbb E_{Z\sim N_2(\rho n_{j,\sigma}+xt_{j,\sigma},I_2)}\!\left[\left\lVert D_p^{1/2}\{\bar\delta(Z)-\delta^F_{j,\sigma}(t_{j,\sigma}^\top Z)\}\right\rVert_2^2\right]\right\}^{1/2}.\] The predicate \(\mathsf{EdgeCert}(c,T_{\mathrm e},U_{\mathrm e},\varepsilon)\) holds exactly when directed rational interval evaluation of \(\operatorname{Eval}(c,\cdot,L)\), the displayed Helmert formulas, and analytic Gaussian tails returns all six intervals \([L_{j,\sigma},U_{j,\sigma}]\) satisfying \(0\le L_{j,\sigma}\le\mathcal E_{j,\sigma}(\operatorname{Dec}(c);T_{\mathrm e},U_{\mathrm e})\le U_{j,\sigma}\le\varepsilon\).

definitions.name: \mathsf{Glue}
definitions.construction: Apply backward induction over nested exposed faces using only the charts \(\Gamma_F\) of \(\mathfrak G\); use the two representative-invariant metrics in \(\mathfrak T_{\mathfrak G}\) as the compatibility predicate and KKT potentials only as computational coordinates.

definitions.name: \mathsf{Cert}_\eta
definitions.construction: Given \(\eta\) and a finite exact encoding of \(\mathfrak G\) with \(p,q\) rational and \(b,\kappa,B,\Omega\) rational or real algebraic, enumerate its exposed-face flags and exact charts \(\Gamma_F\), use minimal-polynomial isolation and directed rational intervals for algebraic constants, truncate the local-Gaussian metrics of \(\mathfrak T_{\mathfrak G}\) with analytic tail bounds, solve rational interval-enclosed finite saddle programs, encode the rounded feasible map as a rational-polyhedral capacity-preserving circuit, and return \((\underline r_\eta,\overline r_\eta,c_\eta)\in\mathbb Q^2\times\mathbb B_{\mathcal A}\).

Let \(\widehat\psi_i\) be the residual bracket in \(\widehat\phi_i\), \(\widehat\chi_i=B^	op D_p\widehat\psi_i\), \(\overline\chi=n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\chi_i\), and \(\widetilde\Omega=n^{-1}\sum_i(\widehat\chi_i-\overline\chi)(\widehat\chi_i-\overline\chi)^	op\). If \(\widetilde\Omega=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d)U^	op\), set \(\widehat\Omega=U\operatorname{diag}(\Pi_{[\underline\omega,\overline\omega]}(\lambda_1),\ldots,\Pi_{[\underline\omega,\overline\omega]}(\lambda_d))U^	op\), using the lexicographically first measurable spectral decomposition at repeated eigenvalues. Put \(L_n^{\mathrm{cov}}=\lceil3\log_2(n+1)+\log_2(8d^2/\underline\omega)ceil\), round each upper-triangular entry of \(\widehat\Omega\) to its nearest multiple of \(2^{-L_n^{\mathrm{cov}}}\), symmetrize, and add \(2d2^{-L_n^{\mathrm{cov}}}I_d\). If needed for the finitely many small \(n\), increase \(L_n^{\mathrm{cov}}\) by the least integer that makes the operator error at most \(n^{-2}\); call the resulting rational positive-definite matrix \(\widehat\Omega^{\mathbb Q}\).

definitions.name: \mathsf{Learner}_n
definitions.construction: Compute \((\widehat\gamma,\widehat\Omega,\widehat\Omega^{\mathbb Q})\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}fitted\text{-}statistics}\). For finitely encoded fixed geometry with rational supplied \(p,q\), run \(\mathsf{Cert}_{\eta_n}\) at \((p,q,b,\kappa,B,\widehat\Omega^{\mathbb Q})\), let \(c_{\eta_n,\widehat\Omega^{\mathbb Q}}\in\mathbb B_{\mathcal A}\) be its code, and define \(\widehat a_n=\operatorname{Dec}(c_{\eta_n,\widehat\Omega^{\mathbb Q}})(\sqrt n\,(\widehat\Omega^{\mathbb Q})^{-1/2}\widehat\gamma)\). A finite implementation first rounds this argument to \(z_L\in\mathbb Q^d\) and then calls \(\operatorname{Eval}(c_{\eta_n,\widehat\Omega^{\mathbb Q}},z_L,L)\). Every returned action lies in \(\mathcal A\), so \(p^\top\widehat a_n=q\) on every sample, including empty-cell events handled by the clipped formulas.

definitions.name: \mathsf{Infer}_n
definitions.construction: Form the \(1-\alpha_0\) studentized joint score ellipsoid for the finite vector \((\tau,\operatorname{vech}(\Omega))\) from the clipped cross-fitted summands in \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}fitted\text{-}statistics}\). For every point in that ellipsoid, run \(\mathsf{Cert}_{\eta_n}\), decode its finite code \(c\), retain every policy map \(\delta\in\mathscr D\) with \(\mathsf K_n(\delta,\operatorname{Dec}(c))\le\eta_n\) under \(\nu_n\), and retain the corresponding oracle welfare \(v_n^\star(P)\). Their union is the candidate set \(\mathcal C_n\subset\mathscr D\times\mathbb R\).

statements.statement: For every \(h\in\mathbb R^d\), the oracle \(s(h)\) exists, is unique, lies in the relative interior of \(\mathcal A\), equals the multiplier construction in \(\mathrm{def{:}oracle\text{-}action}\), and satisfies \(\ell(h,a)=\kappa\sum_{j=1}^m p_j\operatorname{kl}(a_j,s_j(h))\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).
statements.justification: The identity fixes the orientation of reverse KL and turns the policy problem into a strictly convex statistical decision problem.
statements.gap: ClasonLorenzMahlerWirth2021 gives entropy-transport KKT conditions for a fixed cost, while the displayed Bregman identity is the loss reduction needed for an adversarial Gaussian cost.
statements.consumer: Every minimax, face-limit, certificate, and causal-risk statement uses this exact loss representation.

statements.statement: For every one-dimensional face \(F\) of \(\mathfrak G\), use exactly the chart \(\Gamma_F\): actions are \(a_F^0+B_Fx\), \(x\in\mathcal X_F\), observations are \(Z_F=J_F^\top Z\sim N_1(\theta,1)\), the oracle is \(s_F\), and loss and risk are \(\ell_F\) and \(R_F\). This scalar reverse-KL game has an essentially unique minimax representative \(\delta_F^{\min}\); its proper least-favorable priors are locally finite with countably infinite support unbounded in both directions, and its Bayes action is the inverse derivative of \(x\mapsto\kappa H(a_F^0+B_Fx)\) evaluated at the posterior mean of \(\theta G_F^{1/2}\). For the complete binary instance \(\mathfrak G_2\), \(a_{\mathcal A}^0=(1/2,1/2)^\top\), \(B_{\mathcal A}=2^{-1/2}(1,-1)^\top\), \(\mathcal X_{\mathcal A}=[-1/\sqrt2,1/\sqrt2]\), \(G_{\mathcal A}=1/2\), \(J_{\mathcal A}=1\), \(Q=(1/2,-1/2)\), \(H(a)=\operatorname{kl}(a_1,1/2)\), and \(s_1(h)=\operatorname{expit}(h/\kappa)\). Hence \(\delta^{\mathrm{sc}}_\kappa(z)=\operatorname{expit}(\mathbb E_{\pi_\kappa}[h\mid Z=z]/\kappa)\), \(\sup_hR(h,z\mapsto s(z))-r>0\), \(\lvert r-r_0\rvert\le\kappa\log2\), and \(\lim_{\kappa\to\infty}\kappa r=1/8\) in \(\mathfrak G_2\). No affine-rescaling assertion is made for a different one-dimensional face; its inherited result is the preceding exact \(\Gamma_F\) formula.
statements.justification: The scalar saddle reveals that reverse-KL annealing requires an infinite noncompact least-favorable geometry rather than a two-point prior.
statements.gap: Theorem 4.2 of KitagawaLeeQiu2026 has a two-point least-favorable prior and a logistic posterior-probability rule for mean-square regret; the reverse-KL rule is instead logistic in a posterior mean and no bounded-support prior has finite global risk.
statements.consumer: The theorem supplies every one-dimensional residual-face solver and calibrates both temperature endpoints of the global construction.

statements.statement: For every exposed face \(F\), every \(v\in\mathcal N_F^\circ\), and every \(L<\infty\), \[\sup_{\lVert\theta\rVert_2\le L}\lVert D_p^{1/2}[s(\rho v+J_F\theta)-s_F(\theta)]\rVert_2\longrightarrow0\] and, uniformly over \(a\in F\) and \(\lVert\theta\rVert_2\le L\), \(\ell(\rho v+J_F\theta,a)\to\ell_F(\theta,a)\) as \(\rho\to\infty\). For rule sequences, convergence to a face rule means exactly \(d^{\mathfrak G}_{F,L,\rho,v}\to0\) in \(\mathfrak T_{\mathfrak G}\). Consequently \(r_F^{\min}\le r\). The explicitly defined comparator \(\delta_F^{\mathrm{plug}}(z_F)=s_F(z_F)\) satisfies \(\sup_\theta R_F(\theta,\delta_F^{\mathrm{plug}})\le r_F\lambda_{\max}(G_F)\rho_F/(2\kappa\min_{j:a_j\text{ nonconstant on }F}p_j^2)\) for \(r_F>0\), while both sides are zero at a vertex.
statements.justification: The theorem converts every escape direction of the noncompact game into a lower-dimensional decision problem and controls degenerating residual capacities.
statements.gap: Weed2018 controls approach to an optimal face for a finite linear program, but it neither derives projected Gaussian face experiments nor compares their decision risks.
statements.consumer: The face recursion supplies the boundary conditions required by the global gluing question and by certified tail truncation.

statements.statement: In the single experiment \(\mathfrak G_3\) of \(\mathrm{def{:}helmert\text{-}three\text{-}cell\text{-}geometry}\), consider \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{diag}}(\mathfrak G_3)=\{z\mapsto s(\operatorname{diag}(c_1,c_2)z):(c_1,c_2)\in(0,\infty)^2\}\). Every member with finite \(\sup_{h\in\mathbb R^2}R(h,\delta_c)\) has \(c_1=c_2=\alpha\) and therefore belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lin}}(\mathfrak G_3)\); if \(c_1\ne c_2\), the risk diverges along at least one explicitly oriented sequence \(h=\rho n_{j,\sigma}\), \(\rho\to\infty\), with \(n_{j,\sigma}\) given in \(\mathrm{def{:}helmert\text{-}three\text{-}cell\text{-}geometry}\).
statements.justification: The tail obstruction reduces an apparently high-dimensional comparator class to a one-parameter family before numerical separation is attempted.
statements.gap: KitagawaLeeQiu2026 motivates logistic Gaussian shrinkage without aggregate capacity; no cited result characterizes which coordinatewise scalings even have finite risk under exact capacity.
statements.consumer: The result makes the strict nonseparability certificate finite-dimensional and falsifiable in the designated three-cell experiment.

statements.statement: For every fixed framed geometry \(\mathfrak G\), do there exist \(\bar\delta\in\mathscr D\) and, simultaneously, \(\delta_F\in\mathfrak R_F\) for every proper exposed face \(F\), such that \(\sup_hR(h,\bar\delta)=r\), \(d^{\mathfrak G}_{F,L,\rho,v}(\bar\delta,\delta_F)\to0\) for every \(L<\infty\) and \(v\in\mathcal N_F^\circ\), and \(d^{\mathfrak G}_{E\mid F,L,\rho,w}(\delta_F,\delta_E)\to0\) for every strict nested pair \(E\subsetneq F\), every fixed \(L\), and every within-face unit direction \(w\) satisfying the exposing equation in \(\mathfrak T_{\mathfrak G}\)? If so, is \(\mathfrak R\) a singleton in the global almost-everywhere quotient? This worst-risk question is distinct from the posterior-average objective of SunadaIzumi2025 Theorem 3.3.
statements.justification: Existence, nested-face compatibility, and essential uniqueness are the distinct global obligations needed to turn facewise solutions into one capacity rule.
statements.gap: SunadaIzumi2025 Proposition 3.2 selects the unique \(H\)-minimizer over posterior-optimal couplings, and Theorem 3.3 proves average optimality under Assumptions 3.1--3.6. Those results use a different objective and do not establish worst-risk existence, uniqueness, or compatibility across nested Gaussian face experiments.
statements.consumer: An affirmative answer supplies one coherent minimax allocation map for scarce vouchers, beds, or training slots when several target cells lie on capacity faces.

statements.statement: If \(\mathrm{oeq{:}global\text{-}minimax\text{-}existence}\) has an affirmative existence-and-uniqueness answer, then \(\mathfrak R=\{\bar\delta^\star\}\); fix one Borel representative of this unique equivalence class and denote it by \(\delta^\star:\mathbb R^d\to\mathcal A\). No use of \(\delta^\star\) is made without this antecedent.
statements.justification: The binding separates the open existence theorem from notation used in conditional downstream questions.
statements.gap: A minimax representative cannot be named before nonemptiness and uniqueness of the minimax correspondence are established.
statements.consumer: Certified computation, causal attainment, and inference can state their targets without presuming the global minimax conclusion.

statements.statement: Conditional on \(\mathrm{prop{:}minimax\text{-}selector\text{-}binding}\), for every finite exact encoding of \(\mathfrak G\) with \(p\in\mathbb Q^m\), \(q\in\mathbb Q\), and every entry of \(b,\kappa,B,\Omega\) rational or real algebraic, can \(\mathsf{Cert}_\eta\) return \((\underline r_\eta,\overline r_\eta,c_\eta)\in\mathbb Q^2\times\mathbb B_{\mathcal A}\) with \(\underline r_\eta\le r\le\overline r_\eta\), \(\overline r_\eta-\underline r_\eta\le\eta\), and \(d_{\mathrm{EKL}}(\operatorname{Dec}(c_\eta),\delta^\star)\le\eta\), where the inequality in particular requires the extended-real discrepancy to be finite, while also certifying every required \(\mathfrak T_{\mathfrak G}\) face truncation, in time and code length \(\operatorname{poly}(1/\eta,L_{\mathrm{in}})\) for fixed \(m\)? For every \(z\in\mathbb Q^d\) and \(L\in\mathbb N\), \(\operatorname{Eval}(c_\eta,z,L)\) must be in \(\mathcal A\cap\mathbb Q^m\), run in time polynomial in \(L\), the code length, and the bit length of \(z\), and satisfy \(\lVert D_p^{1/2}[\operatorname{Eval}(c_\eta,z,L)-\operatorname{Dec}(c_\eta)(z)]\rVert_2\le2^{-L}\).
statements.justification: A value certificate alone does not recover a decision map, so both a bracket for the minimax value and expected reverse-KL map accuracy are required.
statements.gap: Weed2018 and AltschulerWeedRigollet2017 certify finite entropic programs, whereas the target is a semi-infinite Gaussian game with residual experiments on noncompact face directions.
statements.consumer: The algorithm supplies an auditable fixed-dimensional assignment engine and a numerical error budget for the causal learner.

statements.statement: For any output code \(c_\eta\) satisfying every guarantee in \(\mathrm{oeq{:}certified\text{-}gaussian\text{-}computation}\), define \(\delta_\eta=\operatorname{Dec}(c_\eta)\in\mathscr D\). The symbol \(\delta_\eta\) is undefined when those guarantees have not been proved.
statements.justification: The proposition introduces certified-map notation only after a finite code and its guarantees exist.
statements.gap: An arbitrary Borel equivalence class is not a finite computational output and cannot serve as an algorithmic certificate.
statements.consumer: Later numerical statements may refer to a decoded certified rule with a concrete evaluation model.

statements.statement: In the single Helmert-framed experiment \(\mathfrak G_3\), can \(c_{10^{-6}}\), \(T_{\mathrm e}\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\), and \(U_{\mathrm e}\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) satisfy \(\mathsf{EdgeCert}(c_{10^{-6}},T_{\mathrm e},U_{\mathrm e},10^{-6})\) for all six \((j,\sigma)\), using exactly the displayed \(n_{j,\sigma}\), \(t_{j,\sigma}\), and \(\delta^F_{j,\sigma}\)? Can the same interval computation cover \(\rho<T_{\mathrm e}\), \(|x|>U_{\mathrm e}\), Gaussian tails, and intersections of adjacent edge charts, return a bracket for \(r\) of width at most \(10^{-4}\), and certify \[\inf_{\delta\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lin}}(\mathfrak G_3)}\sup_{h\in\mathbb R^2}R(h,\delta)-r\ge10^{-3}?\]
statements.justification: The unequal-covariance three-cell experiment is a finite, reproducible kill test for both face compatibility and strict departure from common logistic scaling.
statements.gap: No cited Gaussian treatment-rule result provides a certified positive worst-risk gap from every common positive scaling under exact aggregate capacity.
statements.consumer: A positive certificate justifies a coupled solver in the smallest multivariate capacity problem; failure triggers a pivot before causal asymptotics are pursued.

statements.statement: For every \(P_0\in\mathfrak M_m\), the Radon--Nikodym derivative in \(\mathrm{def{:}conditional\text{-}tilt\text{-}path}\) integrates to one. Under \(\mathbb P_{n,h}\), \(\mathbb P_{n,h}(X=j)=p_j\), \(\mathbb P_{n,h}(D=1\mid X=j)=e_j\), and \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp_{\mathbb P_{n,h}}D\mid X\); the supplied quota \(q\) and action polytope \(\mathcal A\) are unchanged. The observed score at \(n^{-1/2}=0\) is \(h^\top\zeta(O)\), \(\mathbb E_{P_0}[\zeta\zeta^\top]=I_d\), and \(\sqrt n\,\gamma(P_{n,h})=\Omega^{1/2}h+o(1)\) uniformly for \(h\) in compact sets.
statements.justification: The lemma makes the least-favorable path a valid causal submodel while holding fixed every supplied capacity and treatment-assignment primitive.
statements.gap: HiranoPorter2009 uses regular parametric submodels abstractly; the normalized armwise tilt here must preserve the finite-cell margins and propensity mechanism needed for exact capacity.
statements.consumer: The causal LAN lower bound uses its information-one observed score without replacing the supplied target masses or propensities by local nuisances.

statements.statement: For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) there are finite constants \(C_\varepsilon\) and \(N_\varepsilon\), depending only on the fixed \(m,K,p,\underline e,C_Y,\underline\omega,\overline\omega\), such that for every \(n\ge N_\varepsilon\), \(P_0\in\mathfrak M_m\), and \(\lVert h\rVert\le M_n\), the \(P_{n,h}^n\)-probability is at least \(1-\varepsilon\) that all three inequalities hold: \[\max_{j,t,k}(|\widehat e_j^{(-k)}-e_j|+|\widehat\mu_{tj}^{(-k)}-\mu_{tj}|)\le C_\varepsilon n^{-1/2},\] \[\left\lVert\widehat\gamma-\gamma-n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\chi(O_i)\right\rVert_2\le C_\varepsilon n^{-1},\qquad \max\{\lVert\widehat\Omega-\Omega\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},\lVert\widehat\Omega^{\mathbb Q}-\Omega\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\}\le C_\varepsilon n^{-1/2}.\]
statements.justification: Finite-cell empirical nuisances remove any unspecified learner and isolate covariance-sensitive map stability as the only nonroutine upper-bound step.
statements.gap: ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML allows generic nuisance learners; this lemma specializes the score to a fully measurable clipped finite-cell procedure with explicit root-\(n\) behavior.
statements.consumer: The expanding-local learner and confidence-set constructions use these exact stochastic errors in their numerical and covariance enlargements.

statements.statement: For every \(P_0\in\mathfrak M_m\), the observed laws induced by \(\mathbb P_{n,h}\) satisfy a \(d\)-dimensional LAN expansion with central sequence \(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\zeta(O_i)\) and information \(I_d\). For every finite \(\mathcal G\subset\mathbb R^d\), \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{a_n:\,a_n\in\mathcal A}\max_{h\in\mathcal G}\mathbb E_{P_{n,h}}[\sqrt n\,\operatorname{Regret}_n(a_n;P_{n,h})]\ge\inf_{\delta\in\mathscr D}\max_{h\in\mathcal G}R(h,\delta)\). Taking the supremum over finite \(\mathcal G\) gives \(r\).
statements.justification: The theorem identifies the exact Gaussian game as an observed-data causal information bound rather than an analogy.
statements.gap: HiranoPorter2009 transfers unconstrained treatment choice through Gaussian limits, but its action space does not impose exact aggregate capacity or the root-\(n\) reverse-KL penalty.
statements.consumer: The lower bound certifies that no observational learner with the same causal information can beat the face-recursive Gaussian value.

statements.statement: Conditional on \(\mathrm{prop{:}minimax\text{-}selector\text{-}binding}\) and \(\mathrm{oeq{:}certified\text{-}gaussian\text{-}computation}\), can the definite clipped finite-cell procedure \(\mathsf{Learner}_n\), for fixed finitely encoded geometry with rational supplied \(p,q\) and with \(\eta_n=1/\log(n+e)\), satisfy \(p^\top\widehat a_n=q\) on every sample and \[\sup_{P_0\in\mathfrak M_m}\sup_{\lVert h\rVert\le M_n}\left|\mathbb E_{P_{n,h}^n}[\sqrt n\,\operatorname{Regret}_n(\widehat a_n;P_{n,h})]-R(h,\delta^\star)\right|\longrightarrow0,\] despite root-\(n\) estimation and dyadic encoding of \(\Omega\) and changes of the active exposed face?
statements.justification: Expanding-local, covariance-stable attainment is the step that converts the Gaussian solution into an implementable sharp causal learner.
statements.gap: AtheyWager2021 supplies cross-fitted orthogonal policy scores and HiranoPorter2009 supplies local decision transfer. DaidoKido2023 derives local asymptotic minimax rules for a scalar partially identified welfare contrast. Sun2026 studies welfare maximization with estimated budget or cost constraints, whereas this question takes supplied masses and quota as fixed. None controls an aggregate-capacity reverse-KL map with nested exposed faces, estimated covariance, and expanding local sets.
statements.consumer: The result gives a deployable locally minimax policy for a planner whose target-cell masses and quota come from an allocation registry.

statements.statement: Conditional on \(\mathrm{prop{:}minimax\text{-}selector\text{-}binding}\), \(\mathrm{oeq{:}certified\text{-}gaussian\text{-}computation}\), and \(\mathrm{oeq{:}expanding\text{-}local\text{-}attainment}\), can \(\mathsf{Infer}_n\) produce \(\mathcal C_n\subset\mathscr D\times\mathbb R\) whose policy projection uses the explicit directed radius \(\mathsf K_n\le\eta_n\) under \(\nu_n\) and satisfies \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P_0\in\mathfrak M_m}\inf_{\lVert h\rVert\le M_n}P_{n,h}^n\{(\delta^\star,v_n^\star(P_{n,h}))\in\mathcal C_n\}\ge1-\alpha_0?\] With \(\mathfrak d_n((\delta,v),(\delta',v'))=d_n^{\mathrm{pol}}(\delta,\delta')+\sqrt n|v-v'|\), can it also satisfy \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P_0\in\mathfrak M_m}\inf_{\lVert h\rVert\le M_n}P_{n,h}^n\{\operatorname{diam}_{\mathfrak d_n}(\mathcal C_n)\ge c_{\alpha_0}\}\ge1-\alpha_0,\] where \(c_{\alpha_0}=2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha_0/2)\min_j s_j(0)\sqrt{d\underline\omega}>0\), and the explicit uniform-tightness quantifier \[\forall\varepsilon\in(0,1)\ \exists C_\varepsilon<\infty,\ N_\varepsilon<\infty\ \forall n\ge N_\varepsilon:\quad \sup_{P_0\in\mathfrak M_m}\sup_{\lVert h\rVert\le M_n}P_{n,h}^n\{\operatorname{diam}_{\mathfrak d_n}(\mathcal C_n)>C_\varepsilon\}\le\varepsilon?\]
statements.justification: Threshold mass makes both the optimal map and welfare nonregular, so a point estimate without an honest uncertainty region is incomplete.
statements.gap: LuedtkeVanderLaan2016RC excludes positive mass at the resource threshold from its regular theory, while WhitehouseAusternSyrgkanis2026 smooths unconstrained policy maxima without exact capacity or nested faces.
statements.consumer: The confidence set lets a resource-constrained planner report both welfare uncertainty and policy instability at the cells where assignments are contested.

sampling_model.design: A full-data finite-cell causal superpopulation model supplies the target mass vector \(p\), the capacity \(q\), and root-\(n\) annealing \(\lambda_n=\kappa/\sqrt n\); the normalized armwise exponential tilt changes only the conditional potential-outcome laws.
sampling_model.units: \(W_i=(X_i,D_i,Y_i(0),Y_i(1))\) are independent under \(\mathbb P_{n,h}\), and \(O_i=(X_i,D_i,Y_i(D_i))\) are the observed draws from \(P_{n,h}\) around \(P_0\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment is conditionally unconfounded given \(X\); the local path holds \(P(D=1\mid X=j)=e_j\) fixed.
sampling_model.overlap: \(e_j\in[\underline e,1-\underline e]\) for every target cell.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Deterministic \(K\)-fold cross-fitting uses clipped off-fold empirical cell-arm means and propensities, held-out augmented scores, eigenvalue clipping, and an \(n^{-2}\)-accurate dyadic covariance encoding. For finitely encoded fixed geometry with rational registry masses and quota, the certificate returns a finite policy code with a capacity-preserving evaluator, so supplied \(p\) and \(q\) enforce capacity on every sample; minimax accuracy remains the certified-computation and attainment question.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat a_n=\operatorname{Dec}(c_{\eta_n,\widehat\Omega^{\mathbb Q}})(\sqrt n\,(\widehat\Omega^{\mathbb Q})^{-1/2}\widehat\gamma),\quad p^\top\widehat a_n=q,\quad\sup_{P_0\in\mathfrak M_m}\sup_{\lVert h\rVert\le M_n}\lvert\mathbb E_{P_{n,h}^n}[\sqrt n\,\operatorname{Regret}_n(\widehat a_n;P_{n,h})]-R(h,\delta^\star)\rvert\to0\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 3.2 selects the unique \(H\)-minimizer over posterior-optimal couplings, while Theorem 3.3 proves average optimality under Assumptions 3.1--3.6.
The paper studies empirical welfare maximization when budget or cost constraints are estimated from data.
Theorem 4.2 gives a scalar logistic minimax rule and a symmetric two-point least-favorable prior under mean-square regret.
The Gaussian limit-experiment analysis yields local asymptotic minimax treatment rules for unconstrained welfare regret.
The preprint develops a locally asymptotically minimax statistical treatment rule for a scalar partially identified average-welfare contrast under directional differentiability.
The resource-constrained stochastic-rule theory does not guarantee estimated population capacity and excludes threshold mass from its regular inference result.
Cross-fitted doubly robust policy learning attains regret guarantees under observational identification.
Fenchel duality gives existence and primal-dual conditions for entropy-regularized transport with finite-entropy marginals.
Theorem 1 gives an explicit exponential objective-gap bound for entropic penalization of a bounded finite linear program.
Sparse Gaussian predictive-density minimaxity under KL loss can require discrete least-favorable priors and strict improvement over plug-in prediction.

tldr: Known target-cell masses and quota define a framed Gaussian capacity geometry whose fixed orthonormal tangent frame determines the covariance coordinates, every comparator, and every escape direction. Each exposed face has an explicit affine action chart, observation isometry, transported oracle, loss, risk, and defined face rule, while representative-invariant local-Gaussian metrics state global-to-face and nested-face compatibility. The canonically normalized scalar game has a posterior-mean reverse-KL minimax rule and unbounded countable least-favorable support. The main open kernel asks for one global minimax map compatible in the displayed metrics, polynomial finite-code value and map certificates, and a six-edge numerical separation in the explicit three-cell Helmert experiment. A normalized full-data tilt, finite-sample regret, clipped finite-cell cross-fitting, and capacity-preserving evaluation retain the causal lower-bound, attainment, and inference program with supplied \(p\) and \(q\).

project_justification.gap: SunadaIzumi2025 Proposition 3.2 selects the unique \(H\)-minimizer over posterior-optimal couplings, while Theorem 3.3 proves average optimality under Assumptions 3.1--3.6; its posterior-average objective is distinct from worst-risk minimax existence and nested-face compatibility. Sun2026 studies welfare maximization with estimated budget or cost constraints rather than a supplied-mass local minimax game. DaidoKido2023 gives a local-minimax rule for scalar partially identified welfare, KitagawaLeeQiu2026 solves a scalar Gaussian fractional rule for another nonlinear loss, HiranoPorter2009 treats unconstrained local decisions, and LuedtkeVanderLaan2016RC studies resource-limited stochastic rules and regular value inference. None supplies the aggregate-capacity reverse-KL game, its six-edge compatibility certificates, or covariance-stable attainment.
project_justification.niche: Root-\(n\) annealing creates a fixed-dimensional Gaussian decision problem in which uncertainty survives on every exposed face at infinity. Known \(p\) and \(q\) make exact feasibility possible, isolating face compatibility and covariance stability as the genuine mathematical obstacles.
project_justification.fill: The scalar saddle and the framed face-reduction theorem lead to three falsifiable obligations stated in one coordinate system: global minimax existence with compatibility in the displayed local-Gaussian metrics, fixed-dimensional finite-code value and expected-KL map recovery, and a numerical certificate on the Helmert-framed three-cell experiment. The same fixed frame enters the normalized full-data path, finite-sample oracle regret, finite-set LAN lower bound, measurable clipped finite-cell learner, and quantified joint policy-welfare confidence set.

related_work: SunadaIzumi2025 is the closest published capacity comparator. Proposition 3.2 of arXiv v2 selects the unique \(H\)-minimizer over posterior-optimal couplings, and Theorem 3.3 proves average optimality under Assumptions 3.1--3.6; these are posterior-coupling results with a different objective from worst-risk Gaussian minimaxity and do not imply nested-face compatibility. LuedtkeVanderLaan2016RC is the closest published resource-limited policy comparator: it characterizes stochastic threshold rules and regular value inference, whereas the present fixed-cell game has supplied masses and quota, positive contact mass, and a local reverse-KL worst-risk target. Sun2026 studies empirical welfare maximization when budget or cost constraints are estimated, whereas this game treats \(p\) and \(q\) as supplied. HiranoPorter2009 gives published local asymptotic minimax treatment-choice theory without aggregate capacity. DaidoKido2023 is a close public but unpublished local-minimax comparator for a scalar partially identified welfare contrast, with neither the capacity polytope nor recursive face games. KitagawaLeeQiu2026 is the closest scalar method exemplar: Theorem 4.2 uses a symmetric two-point least-favorable prior and a logistic equalizer for mean-square regret, while reverse KL changes the Bayes step to a logistic transform of the posterior mean and forces unbounded support. MukherjeeJohnstone2015 informs discrete-prior and plug-in-separation arguments under Gaussian KL risk without sharing the assignment estimand. ClasonLorenzMahlerWirth2021 supplies entropic KKT potentials, while Weed2018 and AltschulerWeedRigollet2017 inform face-distance control and marginal-preserving numerical approximation. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML and AtheyWager2021 supply orthogonal cross-fitting. WhitehouseAusternSyrgkanis2026 informs smoothed value inference without exact capacity or nested faces.
technical_internal_limitation: The scalar tail-splicing argument does not transfer automatically to \(d>1\), because full-dimensional Gaussian sequences centered at \(\rho v+J_F\theta\) retain the transported face experiment \(\Gamma_F\). Equality between the full value and a proper-face value could obstruct a proper least-favorable-prior proof without refuting a global minimax map. The early kill test is the single instance \(\mathfrak G_3\) with the displayed Helmert \(B\) and \(\Omega=\operatorname{diag}(1,4)\); it evaluates all six displayed residuals, their Gaussian tails, unbounded tangential offsets, and adjacent-chart intersections. The angle must pivot if those metric limits are incompatible or the certified coupled optimum belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lin}}(\mathfrak G_3)\).
honest_scope: The scalar saddle, framed face reduction, positive-diagonal tail obstruction in \(\mathfrak G_3\), normalized tilt preservation, finite-cell score rates, and causal lower bound are theorem targets. The binary instance \(\mathfrak G_2\) has the exact chart \(a^0=(1/2,1/2)^\top\), \(B_{\mathcal A}=2^{-1/2}(1,-1)^\top\), \(\mathcal X_{\mathcal A}=[-1/\sqrt2,1/\sqrt2]\), \(G_{\mathcal A}=1/2\), and \(J_{\mathcal A}=1\), yielding the high-temperature constant \(1/8\); no unspecified affine rescaling transfers that constant to another face. Global minimax existence, compatibility in \(\mathfrak T_{\mathfrak G}\), multivariate essential uniqueness, polynomial finite-code expected-KL recovery, the six-edge certificate and quantitative common-scaling separation, covariance-stable expanding-local attainment, and honest joint inference are open-ended questions. The causal layer keeps \(m\), \(K\), \(\mathfrak G\), and the contact configuration fixed; algorithmic attainment requires finitely encoded geometry with rational supplied masses and quota and does not cover unknown masses, an estimated quota, or changing contact sets.
